findings.problem: ShardWorkflow uses bool flags (is_validated, is_sent) and a String status instead of an enum typestate, allowing illegal states like status="sent" with is_sent=false, or both is_validated=false and is_sent=true simultaneously.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid shard lifecycle states are representable and can propagate through the system, causing silent data corruption or incorrect downstream processing.
findings.fix: Replace bool flags and status String with a ShardStatus enum typestate (e.g., enum ShardStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }). Make all fields private behind a newtype. Remove the mutable status field entirely.

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates the input struct in place with mutable field assignments (item.status = ...; item.is_sent = ...) instead of returning a new validated state. No precondition checks ensure the shard can transition to sent (e.g., must be validated first).
findings.failure_mode: Any shard can be marked sent regardless of validation state, bypassing domain invariants. The mutation pattern obscures the state transition and makes the function non-functional.
findings.fix: Design mark_sent as a pure function that takes a ShardStatus::Validated (or equivalent typed state) and returns Result<ShardStatus::Sent, ValidationError>. Move mutation logic to an imperative shell layer that handles I/O if needed.

findings.problem: id is a raw String with no domain type wrapper. status is a raw String with arbitrary values instead of a bounded domain enum.
findings.failure_mode: Any string value can be assigned to id or status, including malformed identifiers or invalid lifecycle names. The domain invariant that status must be a valid lifecycle stage is not enforced by the type system.
findings.fix: Create a ShardId newtype (e.g., pub struct ShardId(String)) with a fallible constructor that validates format. Replace status String with a ShardStatus enum representing all valid lifecycle stages.

findings.problem: All fields of ShardWorkflow are pub and directly mutable. There is no encapsulation or invariant enforcement at the type level.
findings.failure_mode: External code can arbitrarily mutate any field, breaking invariants like requiring is_validated before is_sent. The type cannot guarantee its own correctness.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide only constructors and state-transition methods that enforce invariants. Use a typestate enum pattern so the compiler tracks allowed transitions.

findings.problem: mark_sent has no error return type. A shard that cannot be sent (not validated, already sent, etc.) has no way to express this failure.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid state transitions silently succeed or silently do nothing depending on caller assumptions. No caller can handle a failed transition.
findings.fix: Change the return type to Result<ShardWorkflow, ShardTransitionError> with an error enum (e.g., ShardTransitionError::NotValidated, ShardTransitionError::AlreadySent). The caller must handle the error explicitly.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is Option<u64>, but when the shard is sent, this value must be present. The Option type decouples the timestamp from the sent state instead of embedding it in a typestate variant.
findings.failure_mode: A shard can have is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None, representing an inconsistent state where the shard is marked sent but has no timestamp.
findings.fix: Embed sent_at_epoch_ms directly in the ShardStatus::Sent variant so the timestamp is only present when the shard is actually in the sent state. The type system guarantees consistency.

findings.problem: is_validated is a bare bool that must be manually tracked. There is no type-level guarantee that validation precedes sending.
findings.failure_mode: A shard can transition to sent without ever being validated, violating the domain invariant. The bool flag provides zero compile-time protection.
findings.fix: Replace is_validated bool with a typestate enum where the shard must be in a Validated state (or equivalent) before transitioning to Sent. The compiler enforces the ordering.

findings.problem: No benchmark exists to validate any performance claims about ShardWorkflow or mark_sent. For a state machine module, benchmarking may not be critical, but the Holzman discipline requires evidence for any performance-related assertions.
findings.failure_mode: Without benchmarks, performance regressions go undetected and optimization claims are unverified.
findings.fix: Add a simple criterion or built-in bench target for mark_sent if performance is claimed to be relevant. At minimum, document why benchmarks are not required for this small pure function.

findings.problem: mark_sent uses .to_string() allocations internally. While this is a simple function, the pattern of String allocation for a status value is wasteful and non-idiomatic for a pure core function.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation on every state transition. With the proposed enum typestate, this allocation is eliminated entirely.
findings.fix: Replace String-based status with an enum. The typestate pattern eliminates the need for .to_string() allocation entirely.

findings.problem: No doc comments on ShardWorkflow or mark_sent. The domain intent (shard lifecycle management) is not documented.
findings.failure_mode: Developers cannot understand the domain contract or allowed transitions without reading source or external documentation.
findings.fix: Add doc comments describing the shard lifecycle, valid transitions, and invariants enforced by the type.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for any performance claim about ShardWorkflow or mark_sent
no profiler evidence showing allocation patterns in state transitions
no allocation audit verifying try_reserve or bounded capacity usage (not applicable for this small crate but noted as discipline gap)
no second-ring review or black-hat review evidence
no formal proof plan or verification ledger for the state machine invariants
residual_risk: High. The crate has fundamental architectural violations: illegal states are representable via bool flags and String fields instead of enum typestates, no typed errors for state transitions, no encapsulation, and the functional core pattern is absent. These are not surface-level lint issues but core domain model failures that would allow silent data corruption in production. No commands were run (static review only).
